title: Critical Experience journey candidate
description: One candidate journey in the seven-role grammar (see GRAMMAR.md). Deliberately permissive: only id, name, and source are required. Missing roles are a REPORTED OUTCOME of the resolver, not a validation error — a declared journey with nothing but a name is a legitimate starting point.

name.description: ROLE 1. Business name, not technical. 'Checkout', never 'POST /api/orders'. No inference can produce this — it comes from a human.

source.description: Provenance. `declared` ranks first by default because the customer has already answered whether this matters to the business.

business_impact.description: HUMAN-ASSIGNED ONLY. Never derived from volume — health checks and polling dominate traffic while refunds and disputes are rare and expensive.

aliases.description: Alternate names used to force a cross-source match when normalized names differ.

observed_volume.description: Instances seen in the discovery window. A tiebreaker AFTER business_impact, never a ranking signal on its own.

correlation_key.description: ROLE 2. The case notion. NOT the trace ID — a browser navigation starts a new trace, and async work runs in its own. Highest-leverage attribute in the grammar.

steps.description: ROLE 3. Enumerable and ordered. The enum IS the journey definition — it's what makes drop-off computable.

span_name.description: OPTIONAL implementation binding: the literal Sentry span name for this step. Omit it and the convention applies — `<journey_id>` for the first step, `<journey_id>.<step_id>` for the rest. This field is the SLI-specification-vs-implementation seam: the step id is the spec, the span name is one way to measure it.

evidence.description: For discovered steps: the route, handler, or span name this was inferred from.

outcome.description: ROLE 4. String enum, never boolean — Sentry renders booleans as the strings 'true'/'false', and a binary hides the distinction that matters.

default_value.description: Set at journey start and overwritten on a terminal event, so an abandoned journey is distinguishable from an uninstrumented one.

failure_reason.description: ROLE 5. Bounded, coded, low-cardinality. Never free text, never a raw upstream payload.

magnitude.description: ROLE 6. Numeric business measure. Must be a number — a value stringified as "129.99" cannot be aggregated and is a defect.

step.description: The value-bearing step this attaches to.

actor_segment.description: ROLE 7. Categorical slicing axes. Turns 'checkout is slow' into 'checkout is slow for enterprise customers in the EU on mobile'.

already_available.description: True when it already exists in their auth/tenancy layer and needs no new instrumentation.

excluded.description: Human-marked noise. Drops the candidate from the worklist while keeping it in the record for auditability. Exemptions are first-class here for the reason every service-scorecard vendor converged on them: worklist items a team can never action destroy the artifact's credibility. Discovery will surface health probes, static-asset loads, and polling loops — nothing in telemetry distinguishes a probe from a purchase, so the answer is a one-line human exclusion, not a cleverer heuristic.

excluded_reason.description: Why. Required in practice even though the schema doesn't enforce it — an unexplained exclusion is indistinguishable from an oversight six months later.

needs_clarification.description: Open questions carried into the spec as [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers. The resolver ADDS derived entries for missing roles; explicit entries here are preserved.
